_comments: bc-aidp-next-golive#259 item 1: 'When I create a new Primary Contact, and then search for that same
record under Billing Contact, the name appears twice.'
WHAT THE DATABASE SAYS HAPPENED, because the report reads like a rendering bug and is not one.
vwSalesContacts returns exactly as many rows as it has distinct ids, so the view does not fan out,
and exactly one contact was created that day, so nothing was submitted twice. The two rows are two
REAL contacts: one created by the conversion two weeks earlier, one created by hand minutes before
the report, sharing a display name AND an email. The picker's name field is DisplayNameAndEmail, so
the pair collapses to ONE distinct string -- the rows were not similar, they were identical.
WHY A SECOND ONE GOT CREATED AT ALL is not fixable from this repo. The shared FK picker searches
with an unordered LIKE capped at 20 rows, and on a directory of any real size a first name matches
far more than twenty. The contact that already existed was very unlikely to be on screen when the
picker offered to create a new one. That is a platform defect and is filed as one.
WHAT THIS FILE FIXES is the half that IS ours: the picker rendered a single column, because
Sales Contacts had NO field flagged DefaultInView and the column plan is built from exactly that
flag (minus the name field, the primary key, and any raw foreign key). With one column and one
distinct value, two different people were genuinely indistinguishable -- there was nothing on
screen that could have told them apart, whatever the tester did. Three columns is the smallest
set that answers 'which of these two?' without turning a picker into a grid.
THE FLAG GOES ON THE VIRTUAL NAME FIELDS, NOT THE FOREIGN KEYS, and that is not interchangeable:
the column plan drops any field carrying a RelatedEntityID, on the grounds that it would render a
raw GUID. Flagging LifecycleStageTypeID or OwnerEmployeeID would therefore assert cleanly and show
nothing. LifecycleStageType and OwnerEmployee are plain nvarchar columns the base view already
resolves, so they render as words.
DELIBERATELY NOT Email: it is already inside DisplayNameAndEmail, so a column for it would repeat
the name column and buy no distinction -- which is precisely the case this issue is about.
Lead or established customer contact -- which of two same-named rows is the live one.
Who owns the contact, which is who to ask when the other two columns still do not settle it.
